readings.title: The Offering of First-Fruits
readings.subtitle: A Declaration of Deliverance and Provision
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 26:1] “And it shall be, when you come into the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance, and you possess it and dwell in it,
[2] that you shall take some of the first of all the fruits of the soil which you bring from your land that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, and shall put it in a basket and go to the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell there.
[3] “And you shall come to the one who is priest in those days, and say to him, ‘I shall declare today to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> that I have come to the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to our fathers to give us.’
[4] “And the priest shall take the basket from your hand and place it before the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[5] “And you shall answer and say before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, ‘My father was a perishing Aramean, and he went down to Mitsrayim and sojourned there with few men. And there he became a nation, great, mighty, and numerous.
[6] But the Mitsrites did evil to us, and afflicted us, and imposed hard labour on us.
[7] Then we cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of our fathers, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard <dn>את</dn> our voice and saw <dn>את</dn> our affliction and <dn>את</dn> our toil and <dn>את</dn> our oppression.
[8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought us out of Mitsrayim with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm, with great fear and with signs and wonders.
[9] And <dn>He</dn> brought us to this place and has given us <dn>את</dn> this land, “a land flowing with milk and honey.”
[10] And now, see, I have brought <dn>את</dn> the first-fruits of the land which <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have given me.’ Then you shall place it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and bow down before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[11] and shall rejoice in all the good which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given to you and your house, you and the Lěvite and the stranger who is among you.
[12] “When you have completed tithing <dn>את</dn> all the tithe of your increase in the third year, which is the year of tithing, and have given it to the Lěvite, to the stranger, to the fatherless, and to the widow, and they have eaten within your gates and have been satisfied,
[13] then you shall say before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, ‘I have put away the set-apart portion from my house, and also have given it to the Lěvite, and to the stranger, and to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all <dn>Your</dn> command which <dn>You</dn> have commanded me. I have not transgressed <dn>Your</dn> commands, nor have I forgotten.
[14] I have not eaten any of it when in mourning, nor have I removed any of it for any unclean use, nor given any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, I have done according to all that <dn>You</dn> have commanded me.
[15] Look from <dn>Your</dn> set-apart dwelling place, from the heavens, and bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl and <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>You</dn> have given us, as <dn>You</dn> swore to our fathers, “a land flowing with milk and honey.” ’

readings.title: The Mutual Declaration
readings.subtitle: A Treasured Possession
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 26:16] “Today <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is commanding you to do <dn>את</dn> these laws and <dn>את</dn> right-rulings. And you shall guard and do them with all your heart and with all your being.
[17] “You have today caused <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to proclaim to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways and guard <dn>His</dn> laws, and <dn>His</dn> commands, and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings, and to obey <dn>His</dn> voice.
[18] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has caused you to proclaim today to be <dn>His</dn> people, a treasured possession, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken to you, and to guard all <dn>His</dn> commands,
[19] so as to set you high above all nations which <dn>He</dn> has made, for a praise, and for a name, and for esteem, and for you to be a set-apart people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken.”

readings.title: The Stones of the Torah
readings.subtitle: Building the Slaughter-Place
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 27:1] And Mosheh, with the elders of Yisra’ěl, commanded <dn>את</dn> the people, saying, “Guard <dn>את</dn> all the commands which I am commanding you today.
[2] “And it shall be, on the day when you pass over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn to the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, that you shall set up for yourselves large stones, and plaster them with plaster,
[3] and write on them <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah, when you have passed over, so that you go into the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, ’a land flowing with milk and honey,’ as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers has spoken to you.
[4] “And it shall be, when you have passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn, that on Mount Ěyḇal you set up <dn>את</dn> these stones, which I command you today, and you shall plaster them with plaster,
[5] and build a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> there, a slaughter-place of stones – do not use an iron tool on them.
[6] “Build <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with complete stones, and you shall offer ascending offerings on it to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[7] and shall slaughter peace offerings, and eat there, and rejoice before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[8] “And you shall write <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah on the stones – plainly and well.”
[9] And Mosheh and the priests, the Lěvites, spoke to all Yisra’ěl, saying, “Be silent and hear, O Yisra’ěl: This day you have become the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[10] and you shall obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and do <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> laws which I command you today.”

readings.title: The Curses of Mount Ebal
readings.subtitle: The Twelve Proclamations
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 27:11] And Mosheh commanded <dn>את</dn> the people on that day, saying,
[12] “These are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless <dn>את</dn> the people, when you have passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn: Shim‛on, and Lěvi, and Yehuḏah, and Yissasḵar, and Yosěph, and Binyamin.
[13] “And these are to stand on Mount Ěyḇal to curse: Re’uḇěn, Gaḏ, and Ashěr, and Zeḇulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
[14] “And the Lěvites shall speak with a loud voice and say to all the men of Yisra’ěl:
[15] Cursed is the man who makes a carved or moulded image, an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and sets it up in secret.’ And all the people shall answer and say, ‘Aměn!’
[16] Cursed is he who makes light of his father or his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[17] Cursed is he who moves his neighbour’s boundary.’ And all the people shall say, ’Aměn!’
[18] Cursed is he who misleads the blind in the way.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[19] Cursed is he who twists the right-ruling of the stranger, the fatherless, and widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[20] Cursed is he who lies with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s bed.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[21] Cursed is he who lies with any beast.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[22] Cursed is he who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[23] Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[24] Cursed is he who strikes his neighbour secretly.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[25] Cursed is he who takes a bribe to strike an innocent being.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’
[26] Cursed is he who does not establish <dn>את</dn> the Words of this Torah.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Aměn!’

readings.title: The Blessings of Obedience
readings.subtitle: Set High Above All Nations
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 28:1] “And it shall be, if you diligently obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard to do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> commands which I command you today, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall set you high above all nations of the earth.
[2] “And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>:
[3] “Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.
[4] “Blessed is the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock – the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flocks.
[5] “Blessed is your basket and your kneading bowl.
[6] “Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
[7] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> causes <dn>את</dn> your enemies who rise against you to be smitten before your face – they come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways.
[8] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commands <dn>את</dn> the blessing on you in your storehouses and in all to which you set your hand, and shall bless you in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you.
[9] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does establish you as a set-apart people to <dn>Himself</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has sworn to you, if you guard <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and walk in <dn>His</dn> ways.
[10] “And all peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you.
[11] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall make you to have plenty of what is good, in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, in the land of which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers to give you.
[12] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> opens to you <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> good treasure, <dn>את</dn> the heavens, to give the rain to your land in its season, and to bless <dn>את</dn> all the work of your hand. And you shall lend to many nations, but you do not borrow.
[13] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall make you the head and not the tail. And you shall be only on top, and not be beneath, if you obey the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, which I command you today, to guard and do.
[14] “And do not turn aside from any of the Words which I am commanding you today, right or left, to go after other mighty ones to serve them.

readings.title: The Curses of Disobedience
readings.subtitle: The Consequences of Rebellion
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 28:15] “And it shall be, if you do not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard to do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> laws which I command you today, that all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you:
[16] "Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
[17] "Cursed is your basket and your kneading bowl.
[18] "Cursed is the fruit of your body and the fruit of your land, the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flocks.
[19] "Cursed are you when you come in, and cursed are you when you go out.
[20] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sends on you <dn>את</dn> the curse, <dn>את</dn> the confusion, and <dn>את</dn> the rebuke in all that you set your hand to do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your doings by which you have forsaken <dn>Me</dn>.
[21] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> makes <dn>את</dn> the plague cling to you until <dn>He</dn> has consumed you from the land which you are going to possess.
[22] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> strikes you with wasting disease, and with inflammation, and with burning, and with extreme heat, and with the sword, and with blight, and with mildew. And they shall pursue you until you perish.
[23] “And your heavens which are over your head shall be bronze, and the earth which is under you iron.
[24] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> makes <dn>את</dn> the rain of your land powder and dust; from the heavens it comes down on you until you are destroyed.
[25] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> causes you to be defeated before your enemies – you go out one way against them and flee seven ways before them. And you shall become a horror to all the reigns of the earth.
[26] “And your carcasses shall be food for all the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
[27] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall strike you with the boils of Mitsrayim, with tumours, with the scab, and with the itch, from which you are unable to be healed.
[28] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall strike you with madness and blindness and bewilderment of heart.
[29] “And you shall be groping at noon, as a blind man gropes in darkness, and not prosper in your ways. And you shall be only oppressed and plundered all the days, with no one to save you.
[30] “You become engaged to a wife, but another man does lie with her. You build a house, but do not dwell in it. You plant a vineyard, but do not use its fruit.
[31] “Your ox is slaughtered before your eyes, but you do not eat of it. Your donkey is violently taken from before you, and it is not given back to you. Your sheep are given to your enemies, with no one to save them.
[32] “Your sons and your daughters are given to another people, and your eyes look and fail for them all day long, and your hand powerless.
[33] “A people whom you have not known eat the fruit of your land and all your labours. And you shall be only oppressed and crushed all the days.
[34] “And you shall be maddened because of the sight which your eyes see.
[35] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> strikes you in the knees and on the legs with evil boils of which you are unable to be healed, and from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.
[36] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign whom you set over you to a nation which neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you shall serve other mighty ones, wood and stone.
[37] “Thus you shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a mockery among all the peoples to which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> drives you.
[38] “You take much seed out into the field but gather little in, for the locust consumes it.
[39] “You plant vineyards, and shall labour, but you neither drink of the wine nor gather, for the worm eats it.
[40] “You have olive trees in all your border, but do not anoint with oil, for your olives drop off.
[41] “You bring forth sons and daughters, but they are not with you, for they go into captivity.
[42] “Locusts possess all your trees and the fruit of your ground.
[43] “The sojourner who is among you rises higher and higher above you, but you come down lower and lower.
[44] “He lends to you, but you do not lend to him. He is the head, and you are the tail.
[45] “And all these curses shall come upon you, and they shall pursue and overtake you, until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> laws which <dn>He</dn> commanded you.
[46] “And they shall be upon you for a sign and for a wonder, and on your seed, forever.
[47] “Because you did not serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with joy and gladness of heart for all the plenty,
[48] you shall serve <dn>את</dn> your enemies whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sends against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in need of all. And he shall put a yoke of iron on your neck until he has destroyed you.
[49] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall bring a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flies, a nation whose language you shall not understand,
[50] a fierce-looking nation, which shall show no regard for the elderly nor show favour to the young,
[51] and they shall eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your land, until you are destroyed. They leave you no grain, nor new wine, nor oil, nor the increase of your cattle or the offspring of your flocks, until they have destroyed you.
[52] “And they shall besiege you at all your gates till your high and fenced walls, in which you are trusting, come down in all your land. And they shall besiege you at all your gates in all your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you.
[53] “And you shall eat the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you, in the siege and distress in which your enemies distress you.
[54] “The man among you who is tender, and who is very delicate, his eye is evil against his brother, against the wife of his bosom, and against the rest of his children whom he leaves behind,
[55] against giving any of them the flesh of his children that he eats, because it is all that has been left to him in the siege and distress with which your enemy distresses you in all your gates.
[56] “The tender and the delicate woman among you, who has not tried to set the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicateness and tenderness, her eye is evil against the husband of her bosom, and against her son, and against her daughter,
[57] and against her seed which comes out from between her feet, and her children whom she bears, for she eats them in secret for lack of all, in the siege and distress with which your enemy distresses you in all your gates.
[58] “If you do not guard to do <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah that are written in this book, to fear <dn>את</dn> this esteemed and awesome Name, <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[59] then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall bring upon you and <dn>את</dn> your descendants <dn>את</dn> extraordinary plagues, great and lasting plagues, and grievous and lasting sicknesses.
[60] “And <dn>He</dn> shall bring back on you <dn>את</dn> all the diseases of Mitsrayim, of which you were afraid, and they shall cling to you,
[61] also every sickness and every plague, which is not written in the book of this Torah, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does bring upon you until you are destroyed.
[62] “And you shall be left with few men, although you had become as numerous as the stars of the heavens, because you did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[63] “And it shall be, that as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rejoiced over you to do you good and increase you, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does rejoice over you to destroy you and lay you waste. And you shall be plucked from off the land which you go to possess.
[64] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you shall serve other mighty ones, which neither you nor your fathers have known, wood and stone.
[65] “And among those nations you are to find no rest, nor have a resting place for the sole of your foot. But there <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give you a trembling heart, and failing eyes, and sorrow of being.
[66] “And your life shall be hanging in suspense before you, and you shall fear night and day, and not be certain of your life.
[67] “In the morning you say, ‘Oh, that it were evening!’ And at evening you say, ‘Oh, that it were morning!’ because of the fear of your heart, with which you fear, and because of the sight which your eyes see.
[68] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall bring you back to Mitsrayim in ships, by a way of which <dn>I</dn> said to you, <dq>‘You are never to see it again.’</dq> And there you shall be sold to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one to buy.”

readings.title: The Oath in the Land of Moab
readings.subtitle: A Warning Against Idolatry
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 29:1] These are the words of the covenant which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh to make with <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl in the land of Mo’aḇ, besides the covenant which <dn>He</dn> made with them in Ḥorěḇ.
[2] And Mosheh called all Yisra’ěl and said to them, “You yourselves saw <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did before your eyes in the land of Mitsrayim, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land.
[3] “Your eyes saw the great trials, the signs, and those great wonders.
[4] “But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not given you a heart to know and eyes to see and ears to hear, till this day.
[5] “And <dn>I</dn> have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your garments have not worn out on you, and your sandals have not worn out on your feet.
[6] “You ate no bread and drank no wine nor strong drink, so that you might know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[7] “And when you came to this place, Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon and Oḡ sovereign of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we struck them,
[8] and took <dn>את</dn> their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Re’uḇěnites, and to the Gaḏites, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh.
[9] “Therefore you shall guard <dn>את</dn> the words of this covenant, and do them, so that you prosper in <dn>את</dn> all that you do.
[10] “All of you are standing today before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>: your leaders, your tribes, your elders and your officers, all the men of Yisra’ěl,
[11] your little ones, your wives, and your sojourner who is in the midst of your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,
[12] so that you should enter into covenant with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and into <dn>His</dn> oath, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> makes with you today,
[13] in order to establish you today as a people for <dn>Himself</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken to you, and as <dn>He</dn> has sworn to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ.
[14] “And not with you alone <dn>I</dn> am making <dn>את</dn> this covenant and <dn>את</dn> this oath,
[15] but with <dn>את</dn> him who stands here with us today before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, as well as with <dn>את</dn> him who is not here with us today.
[16] “For you know <dn>את</dn> how we dwelt in the land of Mitsrayim and <dn>את</dn> how we passed through the nations which you passed through,
[17] and you saw <dn>את</dn> their abominations and <dn>את</dn> their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were with them,
[18] lest there should be among you a man or woman or clan or tribe, whose heart turns away today from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to go and serve <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of these nations, lest there should be among you a root bearing bitterness or wormwood.
[19] “And it shall be, when he hears <dn>את</dn> the words of this curse, that he should bless himself in his heart, saying, ‘I have peace though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,’ in order to add drunkenness to <dn>את</dn> thirst.
[20] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would not forgive him, but rather, the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>His</dn> jealousy shall burn against that man, and every curse that is written in this book shall settle on him, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall blot out <dn>את</dn> his name from under the heavens.
[21] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall separate him for evil, out of all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, according to all the curses of the covenant that are written in this Book of the Torah.
[22] “And the generation to come of your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a far land, shall say when they see <dn>את</dn> the plagues of that land and <dn>את</dn> the sicknesses which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent into it:
[23] All its land is sulphur, salt, and burning; it is not sown, nor does it bear, nor does any grass grow there, like the overthrow of Seḏom and Amorah, Aḏmah and Tseḇoyim, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> overthrew in <dn>His</dn> displeasure and <dn>His</dn> wrath.’
[24] “And all nations shall say, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> done so to this land? What does the heat of this great displeasure mean?’
[25] “And it shall be said, ‘Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, which <dn>He</dn> made with them when <dn>He</dn> brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim.
[26] And they went and served other mighty ones and bowed themselves to them, mighty ones that they did not know and that <dn>He</dn> had not given to them,
[27] therefore the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against this land, to bring on it <dn>את</dn> every curse that is written in this book.
[28] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> uprooted them from their land in displeasure, and in wrath, and in great rage, and cast them into another land, as it is today.’
[29] “The secret matters belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, but what is revealed belongs to us and to our children forever, to do <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah.
